Edit 2: The sound mixing is improved, and the starting weapons actually sound like they hurt now. Voice acting seems the same (mostly unconcerned sounding.) It's definitely in a better state and a lot closer to what the game should be, but it's still a bit hard to outright recommend this currently. The game honestly still bare minimum needs better impact, even if that means only more blood or bigger damage impact flashes...

Edit 1 (old): They've mentioned that they're going to update the weapon sounds/animations soon, which should fix my complaints. For now this review remains unchanged though.

Worth keeping an eye on, but I can't recommend it in its current state. Functionally, this is literally Left 4 Dead but in space. You can obtain perks and modified weapons on campaign runs now, but everything else works almost exactly like you would expect it to. Just like L4D there's even no sprinting, you just move fast by default. This all means Anacrusis comes extremely close to being a literal L4D3 as a result, but still has its own identity thanks to its 70s sci-fi theme. These are good things.

That said: The sound design is severely underwhelming to the point where it feels like everything has very little impact, and it never sounds like the characters are actually concerned about anything happening on screen; even when they're dying. The game is also lacking a lot of polish and optimization in general. Since the gameplay mostly boils down to running and shooting (like L4D), it's extremely important to get these elements right since that's basically what the entire experience relies on. I can definitely see this being something special for some people, but there's barely a reason to play this over L4D2 if none of these aspects get improved. Do keep an eye on this one if you're interested in a sci-fi L4D though.
Just made me wish I was playing L4D. Kinda janky and the environments pretty boring.
This is my favorite Hoard Shooter since Left 4 Dead 2, and now has workshop support.

I think this game has potential, which is why I am recommending it. But take this recommendation with a grain of salt because the player count is in the low double digits according to steam stats, which means it's tough to find a game. My full review below:

[b]What I like:[/b]
- It flips the zombie co-op genre by setting it in space
- The music is amazing(though a bit repetitive at times)
- The retro aesthetic and design is pretty cool
- The perks are very interesting
- The grenades are complex and useful
- The weapons have evolved a lot since release. In the beginning they all felt more or less the same, but now they added recoil and different speeds for each weapon
- The pulse is really cool. No need to shove zombies in space :)
- The devs have a discord where they regularly interact with players and read suggestions

[b]What I don't like:[/b]
- The character writing and voice lines. I have no idea who these people are. The only detail I remember is that one of the women was the ship's main scientists. The rest is a mystery. Whereas in a game like l4d2, I know quite a bit about each of the 8 characters. 
- The retro futurism is a bit much. It was created many many years ago, based on the tech available at the time. But compared to the tech we have now, it doesn't make sense. I  refuse to believe that a civilization who mastered space travel could not figure out thin monitors and instead use tube monitors for their computers. 
- There is no score between teammates. The devs seem to think that a bit of competition is bad. It reminded me of those kids soccer games where they don't keep score because it would hurt the losing team's feelings and their parents'.
- There is no text chat. It could be implemented because the 3rd party comms system they use has this feature. They just chose not to, and I think the reason is the same as the point above: to protect feelings. The devs seem to think that if something has even the slightest potential to hurt someone, it has to be removed. But the result is that I am grabbed or goo'd and have to ping like a lunatic because I can not write that I need help. 
- The alien zombies: Their animation is generic. They all act the same, and the way they run is a bit goofy and cartoonish. They also wear very similar clothes and and their faces are covered, which makes sense but kind of dehumanizes them. In l4d2 they had different faces and clothes, which made me feel sorry for them a bit.
- The low player count. I think since an active player base is an integral part of a multiplayer game, this game should be free to play, with paid skins and battlepasses. It's not like players don't have options if they want to play a zombie co-op(old ones with an established player base, and new ones from bigger companies with marketing budgets). No need to add another obstacle for potential players. 


Some suggestions for the alien monsters. Imo, their design is weird and inconsistent with their abilities. 

[b]The Spawner[/b]: When I think of an alien than spawns smaller aliens, I think of something that opens a portal of some sort or teleports them, I don't think of a space chicken that lays eggs. The things it spawns are not great either. What if the spawner just spawned active spikes? They have to come from somewhere, right?
[b]The Gooper[/b]: I would think he has to be big and round to carry all that goo inside, but it looks similar to the spawner
[b]The Flasher[/b]: Evolutionarily speaking, why does an animal that has this amazing ability that's a huge advantage over its pray need to be so big and demonic looking? I would imagine it quite weak and small.
[b]The Brute[/b]: Looks fitting, but is kind of dumb in its behavior. I can easily avoid him so I am not afraid of him at all.
[b]The Grabber[/b]. Nothing wrong with it, just a bit generic and easy to deal with. What if it could camouflage, and it grabbed you but dragged you very slowly(if at all)? The team would have to find the Grabber's camouflaged body to release the player.
I also think it needs more monsters. Something is missing imo.

I went in expecting the game to be pretty mediocre based on reviews from a few months ago, but I have been pleasantly surprised by how much I enjoyed playing through Episodes 1 through 3 so far. This feels like a mix of Left 4 Dead and Back 4 Blood, with the latter mostly coming across in how there are mods for guns, though you have far less (read: no) control over them.

Level design and aesthetics are pretty solid, and some of the new takes on Special enemies are great additions to the genre. Base weapons are fairly limited, but there is enough variance from the random weapon mods and the special weapons to make up for it. I'm very much looking forward to seeing what gets added next.

It's a very enjoyable game, but it needs some tweaks:

1. The guns sound like ♥♥♥♥. They've gotten better with the updates, but they lack that crack that the L4D guns had. I understand that the weapons are sci-fi, but I wish for some better sounds. 
2. The impact of the guns are kinda weak. I like the gibs when you get a headshot, but I wish the gore was more similar in quality to L4D2 (maybe not that detailed, but more feedback would be nice)
3. More weapon variety. The special weapons and grenades are a nice touch, but maybe more weapons, including more than one pistol

The rest of the game is great, I recommend it
I like the potential in this game!

As it is currently deployed this game really misses the mark. It could be so fun but it is tedious, It says a lot of gun updates but there are still the same amount of guns that shoot slow and makes defending against hordes less fun.

4 person team shooter with 70s style and a fun, funky soundtrack. If you liked L4D, you will like the Anacrusis.

Pros:
L4D with 70s style and aliens
Some new and interesting specials (spawners, "flashers" which blow out your screen with bright light, etc.)
In-run systems that allow you to collect perks along the way (these reset after every game)
Cool sci-fi environments: a discotec holdout, rotating platforms, conveyor belts, beautiful geometric gardens...
Option to change into a bot anytime (very useful for those of us with IRL interruptions such as kids and caregiving)
Your turret can have cat ears :3

Cons:
In early access, so it's not completely finished or polished
Quick play always open, which means (currently) randos may join you in your run

All in all I found this to be a fun way to scratch that L4D itch. Recommended!
I especially enjoy it when Mr Sunshine appears.
had some cracking updates over time, keeping an eye on this one

What's not to like!? Shooting zombie/alien things with various types of sci-fi blasters to a disco soundtrack is an excellent way to spend an evening with your three closest pals! I overwhelmingly recommend. It's a blast!
I love this game so much. It's very special to me and you may just love it too.

This game just slowly keeps getting so much better! The current state of the game versus where it was at launch is huge! While it has taken a long time to get there, I think it has been worth it. I definitely recommend this game solely to support the devs but also because it is genuinely a really fun time with friends. Great special Infected, fun weapons that have a surprising amount of variety and precise utility, unique grenades as well as neat perks create a game with a lot of promise. I haven't even talked about the music and the overall vibe of this game which are great, but it isnt perfect. There isnt much to do at the moment and it does take some time for new content to release, but what's here is awesome.
This is a great game, but it has hardly any content.

Wonderful game bursting with potential. Doesn't stray too far from the L4D formula to be risky but what differences it does have fits with it's theme very well. I don't know what it is about this game but I love playing the same 3 missions over and over again.

The story is interesting and I am exited to see where things go from here. Who is Boris? (Some kind if holographic cat AI?) What happened on the Anacrusis? Will our characters go back?

The characters are all great as well. Very well written. Not a whole lot of banter compared to games like Vermintide 2 but what there is has a lot of soul put into it.

The art style has a strong 80s sci-fy theme and the music matches very well. I guess I'm a sucker for bass guitar. I never really watched the old Star Trek show but this game makes me want to for sure.

Game is still in early access so things will change for sure. The fourth mission will be out soon.

Now that the game is 1.0, but a lot of things haven't been fixed. I've decided to completely rewrite this review rather than leave the old one up with a series of updates.

It had potential, and we enjoyed playing it for a while even though it was very buggy and broken: Clipping through objects, buggered enemy AI, a borked matchmaking system. Almost every single time we played at least one of our group would get dropped after leaving the lobby, having to reconnect. The windows store version had/has some pretty major issues on older hardware/slower internet connections. Yet we kept going expecting things to get better.

 Sadly that potential wasn't realized. Instead of a fun co-op pve game with an interesting story it shifted focus towards versus. That story never really went anywhere, and didn't get fleshed out. It dropped the seasons, it slowed on weekly challenges and then started rehashing old ones. Most of the unlocks from these weeklies were removed in their back-end change. (If I had ever lost that much client data in a migration I'd have been sacked.)

There are hardly any actually fun unique weapons capitalizing on the scifi theme Transformers style pew pew lasers, phasers, smart guns, totally not lightsabers etc will not be found here, but if you want a boring minigun or plasma rifle, this game has you covered. 

The pulse could have been fun, but again the devs did nothing actually fun with it. (There are no objects etc to pulse enemies into in a satisfying way a la dark messiah, or even bloody bulletstorm.)

Even though I had recommended and gifted this game to a bunch of people. I can not recommend you pick this up as it is now. For a large part of our friend group interest started dropping when the weekly unique challenged dried up, but losing our earned unlocks just took the fun right out of it.  The other part is that The Anacrusis has a mostly US playerbase, and finding matches is not going to be any fun in European timezones.

Really loved the idea for this game. Old school sci-fi alien blasting action, how can you miss? The aesthetics are what really work for me thematically, the graphics are crisp, clean, and snappy. The game play is your standard shooter nothing fancy which allows you to jump right into the action. The difficulty for a single player is a bit harder than I imagined it would be, but teaming up with a few players definitely evens out the action, while still making you work for it. Overall I look forward to the updates and furthering the missions!
Really fun casual shooter, Good set of modding tools. Devs are also really responsive to community feedback.
